en.title: Global Macro — Korea's chip-export boom meets China's order contraction and an energy import squeeze
en.deck: Korean October exports surged 93.7% year on year, led by chips, but imports became more expensive and China's broad industrial orders contracted.
en.regime: Concentrated AI hardware receipts alongside weak Chinese order diffusion and elevated energy import costs.
en.key_risk: High chip receipts and trade surplus obscure dependence on prices, customer capital spending and energy import unit costs.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2026-11-01 05:00 BRT (08:00 UTC); MOTIR 1 Nov 2026 Seoul release available; US/EU markets last completed Friday 30 Oct.
producer_checks.novelty: Compared 29 Oct Fed/Canada divergence, 30 Oct US GDP versus real household income and AI financing, 31 Oct China PMI/Euro GDP: first full Korean October customs breakdown reveals 93.7% nominal export growth, 259.4% chip sales, 76% daily-adjusted growth, oil import unit price +62.0% with crude volume -6.3%, and geographically uneven destination trade. Distinct price-volume/concentration thesis.
producer_checks.source_check: 14 matching numbered end-references; core 1 Nov Korean trade facts checked against MOTIR original Korean primary release; 31 Oct China PMI NBS; BEA September DPI original distinct from Q3 GDP; IEA September inventories and flows dated correctly; OPEC 4 Oct communiqué not mistaken for Nov 1 outcome.
producer_checks.visual_signature: EN/PT each one evidence table, four charts with exactly corresponding numeric arrays (selected Korean products, Sep/Oct export totals, crude price/volume/value, selected destinations), one three-chain flow, one six-region map.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: Identical 14 reference URLs, same chart series values and units, same sections and conditional scenarios; locale-specific natural prose and chart labels.
producer_checks.research_depth: EN 2572 and PT 2741 words excluding fenced visuals, distinct mechanisms, evidence/interpretation/scenarios, contradictory observations and falsifiers, stock-flow-price-volume separation.
producer_checks.editorial_status: New edition only; no public report or QA approval created by producer.
producer_checks.qa_handoff: Review Korea 1 Nov official release value vs volume, 2026 holiday-adjusted 76% growth, 49.0% derived semiconductor share, 14 matching citations and chart numeric arrays, China PMI diffusion interpretation, oil and OPEC decision cutoff; approve only after SHA-bound independent QA.

contrary_evidence: Non-semiconductor Korean exports rose 34% by value; Korea's overall October exports were below September despite faster y/y growth.
China October PMI below 50 does not prevent sharply higher Korean semiconductor exports to China.
Euro area GDP expanded 0.4% q/q and US Q3 GDP 3.4% SAAR despite weaker household real income.
Crude-oil import physical volumes fell 6.3% even as unit prices and nominal import bills rose.
limitations: Korean customs values cannot isolate chip volume, unit prices, ultimate users or AI customer return on capital.
No Sunday closing equity, bond, currency or commodity prices; latest completed sessions 30 Oct.
IEA September physical Hormuz flow estimate not a 1 November throughput observation.
OPEC+ 1 November meeting not yet verified as final at cutoff.
Country-level credit spreads, capital-flow attribution and food retail pass-through not established.
